SMTO-RST-0005 — SMTO blocked an update that would erase part of a conversation

GUID: e92536e9-11d3-4eb9-92c2-26cdf1bfc983
Slug: run-journal-truncation-rejected
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • An update to this conversation would have removed some earlier messages, so SMTO blocked it. The conversation's saved messages weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation and check that its messages and results are all still there. SMTO blocked the change, so the full history should still be there; this confirms it.
  2. Look at the task's last results to see what it had already done when it stopped. Check whether your action already happened, because the task stopped part-way.
  3. Continue with a new message describing what's still left, rather than repeating the whole request. Repeating the whole request could redo changes that already happened.

What success looks like

  • The conversation shows all its messages, and new work runs without this error.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before you try anything again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; this is a problem inside SMTO. To remove history on purpose, use the conversation's Retention menu once no task is running, not a workaround.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run save supplied fewer messages than the currently retained conversation journal, which would truncate the exact history, so the save was rejected.

What this means

  • A save supplies fewer messages than the currently retained authoritative journal length. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • A save supplies fewer messages than the currently retained authoritative journal length.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare incoming and retained transcript lengths and preserve existing receipts.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Find the caller of MemoryRunStore._save / RunStore.save_in that dropped messages and preserve the existing journal and error details for investigation. Use the supported retention controls only after active and unknown operations are reconciled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported continuation appends coherently; any deliberate retention uses its separate safe lifecycle.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
